record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: For MT, determine axiomatisation and satisfiability results over other mathematically natural classes of metric spaces and topological metric spaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let MT denote the modal language for metric spaces whose formulas are built from a countable set of propositional variables by Boolean connectives and a family of parameterised modal operators $\exists^{<a}$ and $\exists^{\le a}$ (for positive rational $a$), interpreted in a metric space $(W,d)$ via
$$M,x \models \exists^{<a}\varphi \iff \exists y\,(d(x,y) < a \text{ and } M,y \models \varphi),$$
$$M,x \models \exists^{\le a}\varphi \iff \exists y\,(d(x,y) \le a \text{ and } M,y \models \varphi),$$
together with the topological interior/closure operators induced by the metric (so that the language can speak about both quantitative distance and the qualitative topology generated by $d$).

For the language MT, determine sound and complete axiomatisations and characterise the computational complexity of the satisfiability problem over mathematically natural classes of metric spaces and topological metric spaces beyond the class of all metric spaces. Such classes include, for example: bounded metric spaces, metric spaces with a fixed finite diameter, discrete metric spaces, dense-in-themselves metric spaces, separable metric spaces, complete metric spaces, compact metric spaces, locally compact metric spaces, connected metric spaces, path-connected metric spaces, Euclidean spaces $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the standard metric, and metric subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

For each such class $\mathcal{C}$, provide (i) a recursive axiomatisation of the set of MT-formulas valid in every member of $\mathcal{C}$, or prove that no such axiomatisation exists, and (ii) decide whether the MT-satisfiability problem over $\mathcal{C}$ is decidable and, if so, determine its computational complexity.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as an open problem in a list of open problems on modal logics for metric spaces. Subsequent literature by Kutz, Wolter, Sturm, Sheremet, Tishkovsky, Zakharyaschev and others studies MT and related languages over the class of all metric spaces and a few specific classes, but no systematic resolution of axiomatisation and satisfiability for MT across other natural classes (such as Euclidean spaces, compact, complete, or connected metric spaces) appears to have been given. The problem therefore appears to remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: Logics of metric spaces (Kutz, Wolter et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: An axiomatisation of an expressive and decidable metric logic is given; further classes of metric spaces are noted as a direction for future work.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results axiomatise MT-like logics over the class of all metric spaces, leaving other natural classes open.

status_evidence.title: Notes on Logics of Metric Spaces, Studia Logica
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style notes outlining decidability/complexity results and open directions for modal logics of metric spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The question of axiomatisation and satisfiability for further natural classes is identified as open.

status_evidence.title: From topology to metric: modal logic and quantification in metric spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies expressive metric-topological modal logics and their decidability.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses parts of the program but does not settle MT over all the natural classes listed.
